movement_source: row 'Total credit impairment charge', column Year to Sep 24 $m -> column Year to Sep 25 $m
headline: NAB's credit impairment charge rose $105m or 14.4%, from $728m in FY24 to $833m in FY25, lifting the loss rate 1bp to 0.11% of GLAs (ev-1, ev-9, ev-7). The move is entirely a mix shift from collective to individually assessed provisioning. Individually assessed charge rose $328m or 51.6% to $964m — new and increased provisions +$329m to $1,192m — driven by impairment of a small number of Corporate & Institutional Banking customers plus non-recurrence of FY24 write-backs/recoveries (ev-5, ev-2, ev-10, ev-11). This was 68% offset by collective provisioning swinging $223m, from a $92m charge to a $131m write-back, on net release of forward-looking provisions and release of provisions for customers transferring to individually assessed (ev-6, ev-13, ev-14). By division: C&IB +153 to 146, Corporate Functions write-back -83 to 122, B&PB +6 to 529, Personal Banking -33 to 255, NZ -104 to 25 (ev-19, ev-23, ev-16, ev-21, ev-22). Note the statutory impairment note prints FY24 as $741m, not $728m (ev-27). Net write-offs to GLAs rose 1bp to 0.07% (ev-8, ev-15).

drivers.bank_label: New and increased (individually assessed credit impairment charge)
drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: New and increased individually assessed provisions rose 38.1% to $1,192m from $863m (ev-2), the single largest adverse component. NAB attributes it to 'an increased charge in Corporate and Institutional Banking for the impairment of a small number of customers' plus 'a modest increase in charge across the Business and Private Banking and New Zealand Banking business lending portfolios and the unsecured retail portfolio in Personal Banking' (ev-11, ev-12). C&IB impaired assets/GLAs jumped 27bps to 0.33% (ev-20); the presentation names 'Business lending single names' in C&IB and NZ Banking (ev-30). Divisional deltas: C&IB +153 to 146 from a 7 write-back (ev-19); B&PB +6 to 529 (ev-16); NZ -104 to 25 (ev-22); Personal Banking -33 to 255 (ev-21); Corporate Functions write-back -83 to 122 (ev-23).

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Collective provisioning swung $223m, 'from a charge of $92 million to a write-back of $131 million' (ev-6, ev-13). NAB says the FY25 write-back 'was driven by a net release of forward-looking provisions, combined with the release of provisions held for customers that transferred to individually assessed', and QUALIFIES it: 'partially offset by the impact of volume growth in the Business and Private Banking business lending portfolio, combined with deterioration in asset quality across the Australian lending portfolio' (ev-14). B&PB business lending grew 7.3% to $166.3bn (ev-17). Corporate Functions' write-back fell $83m or 40.5% to $122m on 'a lower level of net releases of the forward-looking provisions and the non-repeat of the impact of methodology refinements' (ev-23, ev-24, ev-25). The presentation states 'No underlying collective provisioning charge - volume growth and reducing impact from asset quality, offset by transfers to individual provisions' (ev-31). Collective provision balance fell to $5,002m from $5,165m (ev-28, ev-42).

drivers.bank_label: Write-backs / Recoveries of amounts previously written off
drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: The two credit lines within individually assessed provisioning almost exactly cancelled. Write-backs of individually assessed provisions improved (larger credit) 34.8% to $178m from $132m, a $46m favourable move (ev-3); recoveries of amounts previously written off fell 47.4% to $50m from $95m, a $45m adverse move (ev-4). Net effect -$1m. NAB flags the adverse side inside its individually assessed explanation: 'the non-recurrence of write-backs and recoveries for a small number of customers in the September 2024 full year' (ev-11). Related direct write-off activity: write-offs from individually assessed provisions of $600m in FY25 (ev-29), with net write-offs to GLAs up 1bp to 0.07% 'due to an increased level of write-off activity for the Australian business lending and unsecured retail portfolios' (ev-8, ev-15).

disagreements.explanation: The results book asset-quality and Group P&L tables print FY24 CIC of $728m on the cash-earnings basis (ev-1), while Note 4's 'Total charge to the income statement' prints $741m for FY24 (ev-27), which includes discontinued/non-cash-earnings items excluded from cash earnings. FY25 is $833m on both. The task's headline row is the cash CIC, so $728m is the from_value; on the Note 4 basis the movement would be +$92m rather than +$105m.

disagreements.topic: Framing of the collective/individually assessed split
values: Results book p26: individually assessed $964m vs collective -$131m
Note 4 p53: 'New and increased provisions (net of collective provision releases)' $1,061m
disagreements.explanation: Note 4 nets collective releases into a single 'new and increased' line of $1,061m (FY24 $968m) (ev-26), so it does not isolate the collective swing. Page 26's asset-quality table separates individually assessed ($964m vs $636m) from collective (-$131m vs +$92m) and its four rows sum exactly to the $105m movement (ev-5, ev-6), so it is the canonical provision-type bridge.

limitations: Neither document publishes a FY24-to-FY25 waterfall/bridge chart of the credit impairment CHARGE. The quantified bridge is built from the results book's provision-type table rows (p26), which sum exactly to +$105m; confidence is capped accordingly rather than at walk-chart level.

The only provision walk in the corpus (investor presentation p85, ev-35) is a provision BALANCE walk and runs Mar 25 -> Sep 25 (context), not FY24 -> FY25. Its bars (underlying CP -26, Forward Looking Economic Adjustment +96, Target sector FLAs -185, IAP +243) are NOT drivers of this task's movement and are excluded.

Forward-looking adjustments/overlays are named by NAB as a cause of the collective write-back but are NOT separately quantified for FY25 vs FY24, so no 'overlays_fla' driver could be given a contribution; the $89m net FLA release figure the presentation prints (ev-37) belongs to the Mar 25 -> Sep 25 half, not the full-year comparison.

The collective line is a NET number and NAB explicitly qualifies it: the release from forward-looking provisions and from transfers to individually assessed was 'partially offset by' B&PB business-lending volume growth and asset-quality deterioration across the Australian lending portfolio (ev-14). The volume and risk-migration sub-parts inside that bar are not separately sized for FY25 v FY24, so collective.volume could not be split out from collective.asset_quality.

Divisional CIC deltas were computed by me from the two period columns of each divisional table (C&IB +153, Corporate Functions -83 write-back, B&PB +6, Personal Banking -33, NZ -104; sum +105). The results book states only the Corporate Functions delta in words (-$83m, ev-25); the others are my arithmetic. Divisions are the where-layer, not provision types, so they inform narratives rather than the bridge.

NZ Banking's FY25/FY24 charge is quoted in AUD ($25m vs $129m, ev-22) to be additive with the Group; in NZD the division prints NZ$27m vs NZ$141m, and NAB states FX had nil impact on the NZ credit impairment charge.

Corroboration in the second document is partial: the investor presentation prints Group CIC only half-yearly (p26, p81, p82) and confirms divisional FY totals only for C&IB (ev-33) and Personal Banking (ev-43) via half-year bars; it publishes no FY-on-FY Group provision-type table.

Capped at 80: individual_provisions +329 $m, write_backs_recoveries -1 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
